subject: food-technology
title: Functions of Ingredients: Foundations
welcome_lead: Flour, sugar, fat — what do they each actually do in a recipe?
meta_desc: GCSE foundations on functions of ingredients: flour, sugar, fat in cooking.
final_note: Know the job, know the substitute.

concepts.def: Powdered grain providing structure via gluten.
Wheat protein giving stretch and structure.
Sweetener that also browns and preserves.
Fat blocking gluten for crumbly pastry.

walkthroughs.body_html: Wheat flour provides structure. When mixed with water and worked, the proteins gliadin and glutenin form gluten — a stretchy net that traps gas and holds the shape of bread and cakes. Strong flour has more protein; cake flour has less.
Sugar sweetens but also browns (via caramelisation and Maillard reaction), tenderises cakes by interfering with gluten and acts as a preservative in jams by binding water so microbes can't grow.

Fat adds flavour, carries fat-soluble vitamins, and gives texture. In creaming, it aerates by trapping bubbles. In shortening, it coats flour and blocks gluten development, giving crumbly biscuits and pastry.
